title: KV slab coloring and deferred-eviction quanta for coordinated prefill/decode scheduling
creator: Aisha Gupta
description:
Problem statement: As paged attention workloads scale, small interleaved allocations cause cross-tenant and cross-request fragmentation in the KV cache leading to increased prefill latency and suboptimal kernel choices during decode. Frequent fine-grained evictions create jitter in decode waves and worsen tail latency. We need an allocator and eviction policy that reduces fragmentation, provides predictable residency for decode-critical spans, and allows the scheduler to pick kernels with stable memory assumptions.

Goals:
- Reduce allocation-induced fragmentation by grouping related slots into ‘colored’ slabs (slab coloring) so adjacent KV pages for the same prefill/decode window are co-located.
- Replace per-slot immediate eviction with deferred-eviction quanta: group eviction work into time-aligned quanta that run between decode waves to minimize mid-wave evictions.
- Surface residency guarantees to the kernel selection layer so it can favor kernels that assume contiguous KV spans when residency score >= threshold.
- Provide a lightweight simulator and offline analysis to tune slab size, color granularity, and eviction quantum width per workload.

Design overview:
1) Slab coloring: allocator maintains N color pools (configurable by tenant/priority). New prefill allocations are tagged with a color affinity derived from request fingerprint (e.g., conversation id hash + time-window). We prefer to allocate consecutive KV slots in the same color slab to keep accesses contiguous on GPU memory. Color pools are sized heuristically based on recent max concurrency and average sequence length.

2) Deferred-eviction quanta: eviction passes are scheduled into discrete quanta boundaries (e.g., every 8ms). When a slab exceeds its occupancy soft limit, eviction candidates are marked but physical reclamation is deferred until the next quanta. During the quanta, eviction work is batched and ordered by a combined score (staleness, touch-frequency, tenant-priority). This reduces churn during decode and makes eviction work predictable.

3) Kernel hinting / residency API: the allocator exposes a per-color residency score and a fast API: get_residency(color) -> fraction in GPU. Kernel selector uses residency thresholds to pick between contiguous-optimized kernels (fast path) and scattered kernels (fallback). We add a fallthrough metric in traces showing kernel choice vs residency.

4) Prefill/decode co-scheduling: scheduler aligns prefills to color boundaries and schedules decode waves to start just after an eviction quantum when possible. We add a backpressure token to avoid starting low-priority decodes if a high-volume eviction quantum is pending.

Tradeoffs and mitigations:
- Larger color slabs improve contiguity but increase internal fragmentation. We mitigate by adaptive slab resizing using the offline simulator and by offering small emergency pools for spike allocation.
- Deferred eviction increases short-term memory pressure; we cap deferred reclamation per color and provide an emergency immediate-eviction path when memory crosses a critical threshold.
- Affinity hashing can create hotspots; we periodically rotate color assignment (lightweight re-coloring) during low load to rebalance.

Metrics and targets:
- Target 20% reduction in median prefill latency for long-context requests (>2k tokens) in perf harness.
- Reduce 95th-percentile decode tail latency by 15% on mixed-concurrency workloads.
- Reduce number of kernel-choice flips per request by 50% (measure: how often kernel selector changes between contiguous and scattered during a single decode).

Implementation plan:
- Phase 1 (week 1-2): Implement color-aware allocator and simple deferred-eviction queue in runtime with flags. Add debug traces for color assignment and eviction quanta boundaries.
- Phase 2 (week 3): Add residency API and integrate a single threshold in kernel selector for contiguous vs scattered kernels. Run microbenchmarks.
- Phase 3 (week 4): Offline simulator and tuning harness; run experiments across representative workloads and pick default slab/color parameters.
- Phase 4 (week 5): Integrate prefill/decode co-scheduling heuristics and emergency immediate-eviction. End-to-end canary in staging.

Rollout: staged rollout by tenant priority: internal perf tests -> staging canary -> 10% production -> ramp based on telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: Color-aware allocator integrated with paged KV allocator and can be toggled via runtime flag
Deferred-eviction quanta runs reliably and can be observed in traces (eviction_start/eviction_end markers)
Residency API callable by kernel selector and leads to stable kernel choices in perf tests
Perf harness shows >=15% improvement on 95th decode tail for at least two representative workloads
Emergency immediate-eviction correctly reclaim memory when critical threshold crossed without correctness regressions
notes: 2026-02-26: Spike: implemented prototype color tag on top of existing slab allocator. Observed 10% reduction in L2 cache misses on synthetic contiguous-access workload. - Marcus

2026-03-02: Design review with Research/Serving runtime. Agreed to add emergency immediate-eviction path and limit deferred memory per color. Action: add simulator to choose color_slab_size and quantum_ms. - Aisha

2026-03-05: Perf run (staging) with 8ms quantum, 32KB color slab: median prefill reduced by 12% on long-context model; decode 95p improved 9%. Still below target; next experiment: 16ms quantum and 64KB slab. - Marcus
2026-03-09: PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4837 — implements allocator tags, deferred queue, and traces. Needs kernel-selector integration in follow-up PR. - Marcus

2026-03-11: Security reviewed allocator changes for metadata exposure; no secrets surfaced. Security requested that color tags be non-deterministic for shared-tenant workloads; added rotate-seed plan. - Priya (Security)
2026-03-12: Started kernel-selector integration. Early telemetry shows kernel flips reduced by ~40% when residency > 0.85. Continue tuning. - Marcus
